# Instructor guide · Topic 12: Sorting

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Understand how the classic sorting algorithms work, compare their costs, and use Python’s sorted() with keys like a pro.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **Simple sorts: bubble, selection, insertion:** Three easy algorithms that each build the sorted result one element at a time.
- **Merge sort:** Divide and conquer: split the list in half, sort each half, then merge two sorted lists in linear time.
- **Quick sort and heap sort:** Quick sort partitions around a pivot and recurses; it is fast in practice but O(n²) with bad pivots.
- **Sorting in Python:** In real code you call sorted() or list.sort(): Timsort, stable, O(n log n).
- **Beyond comparisons: counting sort:** If values are small integers, count them instead of comparing them: O(n + k).

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **47 minutes** of guided material (5 lessons)
- Practice: 14 coding problems and 32 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 4 (Arrays / Python Lists), Topic 10 (Recursion & Backtracking)

## Live coding demonstrations

- Keys and stability (lesson “Sorting in Python”)
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Count Inversions: every pair → merge sort** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Sorting algorithms

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Bubble sort?
- Selection sort?
- Insertion sort?
- Merge sort?
- Quick sort?
- Heap sort?
- Stable?
- Python sort?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Bubble Sort (`so-bubble`)
- Insertion Sort (`so-insertion`)
- Counting Sort (`so-counting`)

Code tracing on the board: Sort by two keys (`so-p1`), Stability (`so-p2`), Uppercase first (`so-p3`), Case-insensitive sort (`so-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: Index out of range (`so-d1`), Merge sort loses numbers (`so-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Merge Sort (`so-merge-sort`)
- Quick Sort (`so-quick-sort`)

## Homework

- Kth Largest Element (`so-kth-largest`)
- Largest Number (`so-largest-number`)
- Count Inversions (`so-inversions`)
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.
